name: Equality compares numbers as numbers and everything else as text
why: The definition writes a value as JSON and the record holds it as a typed column. A guard reading `value gt 10000` against a decimal column, and one reading `stage eq "lead"` against text, both have to work — so the comparison picks its rule from the operands rather than from a declared type nobody wrote down.

cases.why: A number written as a string in the definition still compares as a number. 9 is not greater than 10 in text, and a guard that got that wrong would fire on exactly the records it was meant to skip.
A boolean field, which the record holds as a real JSON boolean.
